test_title: PYST 45: SSC GD Constable 2024 - English (Held On: 06 Mar, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
Choose the idiom/phrase that can substitute the highlighted group of words meaningfully.

It's such a small issue. People are unnecessarily making **something unimportant into a big deal.**

options.text: A bull in a China shop
Make a mountain out of a molehill

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"make a mountain out of a molehill"** means to exaggerate the importance of a minor issue. (छोटी सी बात को बढ़ा-चढ़ा कर पेश करना)

 
 
• **Example: **She **made a mountain out of a molehill** by complaining about the small scratch on her car.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Have second thoughts** (फिर से सोचना): Reconsidering or doubting a previous decision or opinion.

 
 
• **Example:** He had second thoughts about quitting his job after he received a promotion.
 
 
 
• **Raining cats and dogs** (मूसलाधार बारिश होना): It is raining very heavily.
 
 
• **Example:** We had to cancel the picnic because it was raining cats and dogs.
 
 
 
• **A bull in a China shop** (नाज़ुक स्थिति में असंवेदनशील व्यक्ति): A person who is clumsy and likely to cause damage in a delicate environment.
 
 
• **Example:** He was like a bull in a China shop, knocking over everything in his path.
 
 

38:Td8a,

The correct answer is: **Option 1.**
